message.content:
Enhance the customer DOMAIN MANAGER for Nxeon at /opt/nxeon to match/beat a modern registrar UX (Hostinger-style). Other work may be happening concurrently — touch ONLY YOUR OWNED FILES.

## PRIMER
Next.js 15 + Prisma. `"use server"` = async-only. `import { db } from "@/lib/db"`; `import { requireUser } from "@/lib/auth"`. Ownership-check every domain op (load by id AND userId). Design: `.card`,`.input`,`.btn-primary`,`.btn-secondary`,`.btn-ghost`,`.table-shell`; `import { PageHeader, Badge } from "@/components/ui/primitives"`. Dark premium theme.
- `Domain` model: `name, status(DomainStatus), nameservers String[], whoisPrivacy, transferEpp, autoRenew, expiresAt, userId`.
- READ FIRST (do NOT edit): `lib/registrar.ts` (name.com v4 signed client — find its DNS record list/create/delete helpers), `lib/actions-domains.ts` and `lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts` (existing DNS add/delete, nameserver, whois, transfer actions — reuse their patterns/exports where possible), and `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx` + any `components/customer/Domain*` components to integrate cleanly.
- The customer's own servers (to point a domain at) come from `db.server.findMany({ where:{ userId } })` — each has `ipAddress`/dedicated `dedicatedIp.address`. The platform public IP is `process.env.PUBLIC_IP`.

## BUILD (reuse the existing name.com DNS record create/delete where it exists; otherwise add helpers in your OWN action file mirroring `lib/registrar.ts`'s signed-request approach)
1. **DNS Quick-setup presets** (`components/customer/DnsQuickSetup.tsx` + actions): one-click bundles that add the correct records —
   - **"Point this domain at my server"**: pick one of the user's servers → add `A @ -> <server IP>` and `A www -> <server IP>` (or CNAME www -> domain). This is the killer feature for a VPS host.
   - **Google Workspace / Gmail**: MX records + SPF (`v=spf1 include:_spf.google.com ~all`).
   - **Email deliverability**: SPF + a DMARC TXT (`_dmarc`), with a DKIM placeholder note.
   - **Google site verification**: a TXT record from a pasted token.
   Each preset shows exactly what it will add and confirms before applying; skips records that already exist.
2. **URL redirect / forwarding** (`components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx`): redirect the domain (or www) to a target URL — implement via name.com URL-forwarding if the API supports it, else via an `A`/`ALIAS` to a redirect note; persist intent and clearly state the mechanism.
3. **DNS import / export**: export current records as a downloadable zone-style/CSV text; import by pasting records (validated, added via the DNS create helper). A route `app/api/domains/[id]/dns-export/route.ts` (ownership-checked) for the download.
4. **Registrar lock toggle** + **Reset DNS to defaults** (with a strong confirm): actions in your file (lock via name.com if supported, else persist + note; reset removes non-essential records and restores a sane default set).
5. **Per-domain checklist** (`components/customer/DomainChecklist.tsx`): a small progress card — registered ✓, pointed at a server, email configured, WHOIS privacy on, auto-renew on — computed from the domain + its DNS + the user's servers.
Mount all of these into `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx` (you are the sole editor) alongside the existing DNS/nameserver/transfer sections, in a clean tabbed or sectioned layout.

## OWNED FILES (create/edit ONLY these)
CREATE: `lib/actions-domains-dns.ts` (`"use server"`), `components/customer/DnsQuickSetup.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainRedirects.tsx`, `components/customer/DomainChecklist.tsx`, `app/api/domains/[id]/dns-export/route.ts`. EDIT (sole owner): `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx`.

## HARD RULES
Never touch schema/next.config/layouts/Shell/lib/auth/db/rbac/lib/registrar.ts(read-only)/lib/actions-domains*.ts(read-only)/worker/ROADMAP/docs or others' files. No build/prisma/generate/restart/commit. No new deps. `"use server"` = async-only. Ownership-check everything. If a name.com operation isn't supported by the current client, degrade gracefully (persist intent + a clear note) rather than failing.

## REPORT
Files created/edited; which features hit name.com live vs are best-effort/persisted; how the "point at my server" preset works; INTEGRATION NEEDED; risks / what needs live name.com testing.

### Live name.com vs best-effort
- **Hits name.com live** (when active + configured): DNS presets, bulk add, import, reset-to-defaults, export (all via existing DNS helpers); **URL forwarding** (`/v4/domains/{d}/url/forwarding` GET/POST/DELETE); **registrar lock** (`:lock`/`:unlock`, read via domain object `.locked`).
- **Best-effort / persisted intent** (registrar not configured or domain not active): redirects and lock state persist to the generic `Setting` KV table (keys `domain-redirect:{id}`, `domain-lock:{id}`) with a clear note; applied live once the registrar connects. No schema change was needed for this.

### How "point at my server" works
`page.tsx` loads `db.server.findMany({ where:{ userId }, include:{ dedicatedIp:true } })` and maps each server to `{ id, label, ip }` (dedicated IP preferred, else `ipAddress`), plus the platform `PUBLIC_IP` as an extra target. The preset lets the user pick a target and www style, previews the exact records (`A @ → IP`, and `A www → IP` or `CNAME www → domain`), and on confirm calls `addDnsRecordsBulk`, which skips any record already present.
